prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation of proteins and RNA organises the interior of living cells into membraneless compartments
For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged, but I have tightened the wording after round 1. B065 is the one shortlisted achievement that gave chemistry a new concept of molecular organisation: multivalent biopolymers demix into dense and dilute liquid phases, and cells use this to build compartments without membranes. The founding observation is the 2009 P-granule work of Hyman and Brangwynne, and the citation rests only on that demonstrated, reproducible phenomenon, not on any claim that every reported condensate is an equilibrium phase. B011 is the best-supported and cleanest-attributed methodological achievement on the list, with the highest opening support, independent replication and early clinical use. In answer to the chair's question, the chemical discovery that a Liu-only citation honours is the programmed, single-nucleotide chemical conversion of a base (C to U, and A to I by an evolved deaminase) in genomic DNA without a double-strand break, made possible by directed evolution of the deaminase. That is a chemical transformation designed and optimised at a precise site, not the cleavage-and-repair mechanism the 2020 prize recognised. Together the two parts honour a concept and a tool, from physical chemistry of life and from chemical biology.
statement.case_against: The costs are unchanged and I accept them. Rosen, whose 2012 multivalent-interaction work gave the quantitative in vitro basis of phase separation, and Pappu and Mittag, who supplied the sequence grammar, are left out, and only the three-person cap forces this once Liu is included. B065 is also the least mature candidate on the shortlist: no other member ranks it first, and Aili, Aqvist, Somfai and Chabes all say the condensate debate should settle first. A Liu-only credit leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, and the Target-AID priority question is not resolved. Base editing sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and a two-part prize of such different topics may look like a compromise, which is a presentation risk I do not dismiss.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that a prize should reward what is settled, that the condensate concept is still being argued, and that he would revisit phase separation in a later year. He holds base editing as the whole prize, with Liu alone.
responses.response: I agree with the principle, and I agree with you on Liu alone, which is why the B011 part now matches your credit. Where I differ is on what is unsettled. What is open is which individual condensates are equilibrium phases and how much of their function depends on it. What is settled is that proteins and RNA phase separate in vitro and in cells, that this follows binodal and multivalency rules, and that it reorganised a decade of cell biology. A citation for the concept covers only the second. I would also accept a second part for base editing only if the committee is satisfied that it differs from CRISPR editing, and your one-sentence formulation of programmed base deamination plus deaminase evolution is the best I have seen, so I used it.

responses.point: Somfai respects the physical chemistry but says the settled core, multivalent assembly in vitro, is narrower than the headline concept, and he would revisit phase separation in a few years.
responses.response: This is the strongest objection, and it is partly right: the most quantitative settled part is Rosen's in vitro multivalency work, which a Hyman and Brangwynne citation does not name. But the concept entered the field through the cellular observation, and a citation that says 'organises the interior of living cells' is true of that observation. If the committee finds the narrower core more defensible, the honest alternative is a B065 prize with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, not deferral. Waiting does not make Rosen's credit easier, since the cap problem will remain. On your own configuration, I find the Crews-only credit under B038 hard to defend against Deshaies and Ciulli, which is why I do not follow you there.

responses.point: Chabes accepts Liu alone as workable but wants the condensate question resolved by quantitative measurement in cells before ranking B065 above degraders. He ranks degraders first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli.
responses.response: The measurement point is fair, and quantitative cell measurements of dense and dilute phase concentrations and material properties do exist for several systems, although not for all. On B038, I find your Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio scientifically convincing as a PROTAC citation, and it remains my first alternative. What keeps me from moving it into my configuration is that a PROTAC-only citation leaves the cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) unrecognised, and no degrader is yet approved. If the committee writes a narrowly framed PROTAC citation, I could accept it, but I do not see a majority forming around the credit split.

responses.point: Aili finds the condensate concept exciting but early, and would place it below candidates whose chemical claims are settled; she ranks degraders first.
responses.response: I understand this, and my preference for the concept does not rest on the debate being over. My position differs from yours on timing only: the founding observation is fifteen years old, tested in many laboratories, and the debate is about interpretation, not about whether the phenomenon exists. I do share your concern on the chair's question about maturity. I would weigh no approved degrader and incomplete off-target characterisation of base editing as comparable, partial maturity costs, rather than reasons to rank B038 or B011 above settled work.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards phase separation as mature enough, since no other member has it as a first choice and the concept-level wording may not satisfy those who want the in vitro core named.

Whether Rosen should replace Brangwynne or Liu within the three-person limit, or whether a single-part B065 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is more defensible; I have not moved because the two-part prize with Liu has more support overall.
Whether the Target-AID priority of Nishida and Kondo changes the Liu-only credit, and how much off-target and bystander deamination weighs against maturity.
I rely on memory of the literature and have not checked the credit record or clinical status.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any credited candidate. My research on lipid self-assembly and on lipid-protein co-assembly in amyloid is scientifically close to B065, and B018 (lipid nanoparticles), which is one of my alternatives, is close to my own field. I disclose this proximity, and I continue to judge that it does not require recusal. I would abstain from weighing B018 as a preferred part.
